Ordering case 1: the same host in two feeds belongs to the EARLIER member. Order [X,Y]: Y keeps only 3.3.3.3. Reversed order (rec_own_dup_reversed) moves 2.2.2.2 to Y and X loses it; a translator that iterates the other way, or keeps the later owner, gets that other answer here.
Ordering case 1 (reverse of rec_own_dup_earlier_wins): order [Y,X] gives 2.2.2.2 to Y and leaves X with 1.1.1.1 only.

Ordering case 1, contained variant: earlier /24, later host inside it: the later feed LOSES the host (Y empty). Reversed (rec_own_host_then_cidr) the later /24 is only partially covered by the host and is kept whole; a wrong order or a partial-cover prune gives Y empty there instead.

Ordering case 1, contained variant (reverse): earlier host, later /24: the /24 stays whole (issue #3606: only full containment prunes), so both feeds keep their row; the wrong order would prune the host from X instead.

Ordering case 2 (v4): suppression runs after a sibling-triggered recompute. Pass 1 parses both feeds and suppresses 203.0.113.5 from AliasA. Pass 2 changes ONLY feed B: recompute rewrites AliasA's deny file from its pre-suppression snapshot, and the suppression pass must run again for AliasA (recompute ran). A translator that suppresses only changed feeds puts 203.0.113.5 back into AliasA's canonical set in pass 2.
Ordering case 2 (v6): as pipe_sibling_recompute_v4 for IPv6 (dedup on so v6 recomputes).
Ordering case 2 control: dedup off and no reputation: no recompute runs in pass 2, so the suppressed alias keeps its pass-1 suppressed file and the canonical set still excludes the host.

Ordering case 2, single pass: pMax (max=3) crosses its threshold only WITH the suppressed host counted (four hosts). Order of the old path: recompute collapses to 203.0.113.0/24, THEN suppression cuts .4 out of it, leaving 8 covering entries that exclude .4. A translator that suppresses first sees three hosts, never collapses, and returns the three hosts.
Ordering case 2, single pass with dMax: as pipe_suppress_after_pmax (unknown country, ccblack=block).
Ordering case 2, dedup off: only the rep trigger routes recompute; suppression still follows it.
Both dRep and pRep on: recompute applies dMax, then the legacy pMax verb runs over the emitted deny files, then suppression.

Ordering case 4 (v4): the only member is fully suppressed: the canonical set is [] (a real empty set), and closing then refills the deny file with the placeholder. A translator that substitutes the placeholder in the canonical set, or keeps the previous content, differs.
Ordering case 4 (v6): as pipe_all_suppressed_v4 for IPv6.
